title.narrative: Regional and sub-regional constituents have strengthened institutional capacities for improved productivity growth in Africa including inclusive transformation for decent work in the informal economy

description.narrative: The informal economy in Africa remains large and continues to expand, with self-employment—often in vulnerable and low-productivity activities—predominating, particularly in labour-intensive service sectors. This contributes to persistent decent work deficits, including low incomes, limited access to finance, weak productivity, and high levels of poverty and inequality. This Regional Outcome contributes to the result of strengthened capacity of ILO constituents to design and implement integrated, inclusive and results-oriented policies and programmes that accelerate the transition to formality. It supports the development of a Global Roadmap on the Transition to Formality for Decent Work (2027–2032), in line with the mandate of the International Labour Conference (ILC 2025) and ILO Recommendation No. 204. To achieve this outcome, the following outputs are delivered: Capacity of the ILO tripartite constituents in Africa strengthened through subregional tripartite consultations and policy dialogue to develop frameworks reflecting the diverse nature and drivers of informality; knowledge base on transition to formality strengthened through the production and dissemination of analytical and research products; enterprise productivity enhanced through support to micro, small and medium-sized enterprises (MSMEs), including technology adoption and improved management practices; and access to financial services improved through strengthened coordination platforms and networks among microfinance institutions. It also contributes to strengthened evidence-based policymaking, including in the areas of social security agreements, digitalization of labour-related services, and skills and lifelong learning systems. Together, these outputs contribute to improved policy coherence, enhanced institutional capacity and more effective pathways to formalization, leading to better working conditions, increased productivity and sustainable enterprise development.
